stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dP}{dt} = 3 P - 6 t^{2} \). Without drawing it, describe the field of slope segments for this equation: where the segments are horizontal, where they have positive slope, and where they have negative slope.

answer_key.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( P = 2 t^{2} \), have positive slope where \( P > 2 t^{2} \), and have negative slope where \( P < 2 t^{2} \).

worked_solution.text: A segment is horizontal where the right side is 0: \( 3 P - 6 t^{2} = 0 \) exactly when \( P = 2 t^{2} \), which is the parabola \( P = 2 t^{2} \).
The right side equals \( 3\left(P - 2 t^{2}\right) \), so its sign is positive where \( P > 2 t^{2} \) and negative where \( P < 2 t^{2} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the slope on each side of the locus

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( t = 2 P^{2} \), have positive slope where \( t > 2 P^{2} \), and have negative slope where \( t < 2 P^{2} \).
options.derivation: each lattice point read with its coordinates exchanged, so t and P trade places

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( P = 0 \), have positive slope where \( P > 0 \), and have negative slope where \( P < 0 \).
options.derivation: the slope read as depending on P alone, the t term ignored, so the segments would match along horizontal lines

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the parabola \( P = 2 t^{2} \), have positive slope where \( P < 2 t^{2} \), and have negative slope where \( P > 2 t^{2} \).
options.derivation: the horizontal row located but the tilt on each side taken from the look of a familiar field instead of from a computed slope
